name: Unwritten Rules for First-Timers
why_it_works: First-timers stay away from a scene because they are afraid of doing something wrong in front of regulars. Naming the unwritten rules removes that fear, makes {{brand}} the friendly host, and gives regulars a list they recognize and want to share with newcomers.

hook.pattern: Speak to a nervous first-timer and promise the rules regulars never say out loud.
examples: Rules regulars never say out loud. Learn them here.
Rule four is the one every newcomer breaks.

variables.name: scene
variables.description: The place or event a first-timer is nervous about; 4 words or fewer

variables.name: rule_1
variables.description: First unwritten rule, the easiest one; starts with a verb, 7 words or fewer
variables.example: ask before you touch a car

variables.name: why_1
variables.description: Why rule 1 matters, one plain sentence that starts with a capital letter
variables.example: Some of these paint jobs took three years.

variables.name: rule_2
variables.description: Second unwritten rule; starts with a verb, 7 words or fewer

variables.name: why_2
variables.description: Why rule 2 matters, one plain sentence that starts with a capital letter
variables.example: Those spots are saved for cars on display.

variables.name: rule_3
variables.description: Third unwritten rule; starts with a verb, 7 words or fewer
variables.example: compliment the build, not the price

variables.name: why_3
variables.description: Why rule 3 matters, one plain sentence that starts with a capital letter
variables.example: Owners love talking about the work, not the cost.

variables.name: rule_4
variables.description: The rule newcomers break most often; starts with a verb, 7 words or fewer
variables.example: step back when a car hops

variables.name: why_4
variables.description: Why rule 4 matters, one plain sentence that starts with a capital letter
variables.example: A hopping car can land a foot from where it started.

variables.name: bring_list
variables.description: What a first-timer should bring, as a short comma list that starts with a capital letter
variables.example: A folding chair, water, cash for the food trucks

variables.name: first_move
variables.description: The best thing to do in the first ten minutes, one sentence that starts with a capital letter
variables.example: Find a club tent and ask who built what.

variables.name: event
variables.description: Where to try the rules in person; 6 words or fewer
variables.example: our Sunday meet at Elm Park

craft.technique: Etiquette list with a common-mistake finale
craft.notes: Order the rules from easiest to the one newcomers break, so the last rule pays off the hook. Keep the tone of a friendly host, never a gatekeeper; every rule should make the viewer more likely to show up, not less.

do_not: Make rules that sound like the scene does not want newcomers
Invent rules regulars would not recognize; they will correct you publicly
Use slang or customs from a culture the brand is not part of
